mainTopic: Shared responsibility for a dangerous pit: deadly fumes, partners handing over a בור, ברירה, and acquiring a בור with its bucket
overview: This amud is about a dangerous pit (בור) that more than one person helped make, and about who is responsible for it. First the גמרא tries to explain two ברייתות about a pit that several people worked on, using the מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן. רב זביד shows that both ברייתות can follow one view, with the idea of deadly fumes (הבל) explaining the plastering case. רבא then adds that building up a pit's rim to ten טפחים is the same as digging. He also asks what happens if the second person undoes his addition, and that question stays a תיקו. Next come rulings about how water and width affect a pit's deadly fumes, including two more תיקו questions and רב אשי's answer about a pit that was widened. The גמרא then asks when a partner who leaves an uncovered בור stops being responsible. It connects that question to the idea of ברירה, which also explains partners who made a נדר about their shared חצר. Finally, רבי אלעזר teaches that handing over the bucket lets a buyer acquire a בור through חזקה. רבי יהושע בן לוי then begins a ruling about selling a house, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Do the two ברייתות follow רבי and רבנן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא saying everyone is liable follows רבי, and the one saying only the last is liable follows רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this ברייתא follows רבי, and that ברייתא follows רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a simple way to explain why the two ברייתות give different rulings. It is setting up the next move, where רב זביד will reject this suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that when one person dug part of a pit and another finished it, both can be liable. רבנן hold that only the last one is liable. So it looks natural to say the 'everyone is liable' ברייתא is רבי and the 'last one is liable' ברייתא is רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will usually reject)

steps.confusionAlert: לימא is not a final answer. It is a test balloon that the גמרא usually pops right away.

phrases.english: Shall we say this one is Rabbi,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ברייתא that says everyone who deepened the pit is liable.

phrases.english: and that one is the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Connects the two ברייתות quoted earlier to the רבי / רבנן מחלוקת about digging nine and then ten טפחים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the two ברייתות really argue, following רבי and רבנן.

steps.title: רב זביד: both ברייתות follow רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבנן only make the last person alone liable when the first did not dig a pit deep enough to kill. If the first already made a deadly pit, even רבנן agree everyone is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: Both follow רבנן. רבנן only said the last one is liable when the first did not make a pit deep enough to kill. But when the first did make it deep enough to kill, even רבנן agree that all of them are liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד rejects the idea that the ברייתות argue. He shows how both can fit the view of רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן ruling (only the last is liable) applies when the first person dug less than the deadly depth of ten טפחים. In the first ברייתא, the first person already dug a deadly pit, so the others only added to an existing danger. In that case even רבנן agree that everyone is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: They only said their ruling (in this limited case)
The measure that causes death (a pit ten טפחים deep)

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said:
This one and that one are both the Rabbis;
the Rabbis only said
that the last one is liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּלָא עֲבַד קַמָּא שִׁיעוּר מִיתָה;
phrases.english: where the first one did not make it the measure for death;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דַּעֲבַד קַמָּא שִׁיעוּר מִיתָה –
phrases.english: but where the first one did make it the measure for death,
even the Rabbis agree that they are all liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: הָא וְהָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the לימא suggestion by limiting how far the רבנן ruling reaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the רבנן ruling applies only when the first pit was not yet deadly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות argue, following רבי and רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both follow רבנן; the first ברייתא is a case where the first person already made a deadly pit.

steps.title: Challenge from the plastering case
steps.stepSummary: In the plastering ברייתא the first person also made a deadly pit, yet only the last is liable. That seems to contradict רב זביד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the case where he plastered and cemented the pit, the first one did make it deep enough to kill, and still it teaches that only the last one is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב זביד's answer using the second ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plastering and cementing only work on a pit that is already dug. So the first person's pit was already deep enough to kill. By רב זביד's rule, everyone should be liable, yet that ברייתא says only the last one is.

keyTerms.meaning: He plastered and cemented (the walls of the pit)

phrases.english: But there is the case where he plastered and cemented,
where the first one did make it the measure for death,
and it teaches: the last one is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב זביד's rule using the second ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב זביד's claim that when the first pit is deadly, even רבנן hold everyone liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the plastering case the first pit was already deadly, yet only the last person is liable.

steps.title: The plastering created the deadly fumes
steps.stepSummary: In the plastering case the original pit had no deadly fumes. The plastering made it narrow enough to hold fumes that kill, so the last person created the danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answered: There, the pit had no fumes that could kill. Then another person came and added fumes that could kill.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב זביד by explaining that the plastering case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit kills partly through its suffocating fumes (הבל). In that case the first pit was so wide that it had no deadly fumes. Plastering narrowed it and created deadly fumes, so the last person is the one who made it a killing pit.

keyTerms.meaning: Fumes or stifling air inside a pit

phrases.english: They said: There,
it had no fumes for death,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא אַחֵר וְהוֹסִיף בָּהּ הֶבֶל לְמִיתָה.
phrases.english: and another came and added to it fumes for death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ הֶבֶל לְמִיתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by showing the first pit was not actually deadly.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: deadly fumes, not just depth, were missing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first pit in the plastering case was already deadly.
steps.terutzMaskana: It lacked deadly fumes. The plasterer created the deadly danger, so only he is liable.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this version, both ברייתות follow רבנן. Everyone is liable if the first pit was already deadly; only the last is liable if he is the one who made it deadly, whether through depth or fumes.

steps.title: Second version: both ברייתות follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains both according to רבי. The first ברייתא fits easily, and the plastering case is one where the first pit had no fumes for death or for damage at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רב זביד said: Both follow רבי. The one that teaches 'they are all liable' fits well. The one that teaches 'the last one is liable' is a case where the pit had no fumes at all, neither for death nor for damage. Then another person came and added fumes for both death and damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of רב זביד's answer, explaining both ברייתות according to רבי instead of רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי already holds that several people can share liability, so the first ברייתא matches him with no difficulty. To explain why רבי makes only the last person liable in the plastering case, רב זביד says the original pit had no harmful fumes at all, not even enough to cause injury. Since the first person contributed nothing harmful, only the plasterer is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב זביד. Either both ברייתות follow רבנן (steps 2-4) or both follow רבי. In both versions they do not truly argue: the plastering case is one where the first pit lacked the relevant fumes.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix the two versions. In the רבי version, the first pit lacked fumes even for damage, not only for death.

phrases.english: There are those who say, Rav Zevid said:
This one and that one are both Rabbi;
this one that teaches 'they are all liable' is fine;
that one which teaches 'the last one is liable'
is a case where it had no fumes
neither for death nor for damages,
and another came and added fumes to it
both for death and for damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב זְבִיד: הָא וְהָא רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the לימא in step 1, using רבי instead of רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case to fit רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'last one is liable' ברייתא must follow רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: It fits רבי too, because the first pit had no harmful fumes of any kind.

steps.title: Raising the pit from the top also counts
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if someone puts a stone at the edge of a shallow pit and brings it to ten טפחים, this is the same case as the מחלוקת between רבי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: If someone placed a stone at the opening of a pit and so brought it up to ten טפחים, we have reached the argument between רבי and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new case. The second person does not dig deeper. He builds the pit up from the top with a stone, and רבא says this is the same as the argument we have been learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the second person made the pit deeper by digging. Here the pit was less than ten טפחים, and a stone on the rim makes the total height ten, which is deep enough to kill. רבא says this counts as 'completing the pit' just like digging, so the same מחלוקת applies.

keyTerms.meaning: And completed it to ten טפחים, the depth that can kill
We have arrived at the argument

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one placed a stone at the opening of the pit,
phrases.notes: The pit was less than ten טפחים deep, and the stone on the rim adds the missing height.

phrases.english: and brought it up to ten handbreadths –
we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi and the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: This is the argument from the earlier steps: is only the last person liable, or are both?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הִנִּיחַ אֶבֶן עַל פִּי הַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the רבי/רבנן dispute and applies it to a new way of completing the pit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding height at the top of a pit with a stone to reach ten טפחים is treated like digging, and falls under the מחלוקת רבי ורבנן.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this, since it looks like the very same case.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's statement as too obvious to need saying. This sets up the next step, which explains what רבא is really teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the pit reached ten טפחים because of the second person, why should it matter whether he added at the top or the bottom? The challenge pushes us to find what new point רבא's statement adds.

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether רבא's ruling adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Raising a pit to ten טפחים looks exactly like the case already argued about, so the statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The deadly air is not his, yet he is still included
steps.stepSummary: One might think that adding from the top does not count, because the deadly air at the bottom was not made by him. רבא teaches that it still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: when he digs at the bottom, it is his own deadly air that kills. But when he adds at the top, the deadly air that kills is not his, so say he is not responsible. רבא teaches us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It shows there was a real reason to think the top case is different, and רבא tells us it is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal in a pit dies from the bad air (הבלא) at the bottom. If the second person dug at the bottom, he made that deadly air himself. If he only added a stone at the top, the air at the bottom was already there, so we might have said he did not cause the death. רבא teaches that making the pit reach ten טפחים is enough to place him inside the מחלוקת.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces the mistaken assumption)
The bad, suffocating air in a pit that kills
At the bottom / at the top
It teaches us (that the assumption is wrong)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the stone-placer might go free. Under both רבי and רבנן the last person, the one who completed the pit to ten, is liable. The argument is only about whether the first digger is also liable.

phrases.english: Lest you say,

phrases.aramaic: לְמַטָּה הוּא דְּהַבְלָא דִידֵיהּ קָא קָטֵיל לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: at the bottom, it is his own fumes that kill it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the animal that fell in. Digging deeper at the bottom creates new deadly air.

phrases.english: but at the top –
where it is not his fumes that kill,
say he is not liable;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by showing the חידוש in רבא's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a real reason one might have ruled differently (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Adding at the top should not count, since the deadly air at the bottom is not his.
steps.terutzMaskana: Completing the pit to ten טפחים from the top counts too, and falls into the מחלוקת רבי ורבנן.
steps.whatToRemember: Bringing a pit to ten טפחים counts, whether you dig deeper at the bottom or build up the rim at the top.

steps.title: What if the second person undoes his addition?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks: if the second person closes up the handbreadth he dug, or removes his stones, who is now responsible for the pit?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: If he filled in the טפח he dug, or took away his stones, what is the law? Do we say he simply took back what he did, so things return to how they were? Or do we say the first person's act was removed, and the whole pit now stands under his responsibility?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question about the second person undoing his own work. He lays out two possible ways to look at it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the second person just removed his own addition, so the first digger is responsible again, as before. Side two: when the second person completed the pit, the first digger's act was swallowed up and the pit became fully his. Undoing his part does not bring the first person back, so the second person stays responsible for the whole pit.

keyTerms.meaning: He filled in or plastered over a handbreadth
What he did, he took back
The first person's act has been removed
In his domain, under his responsibility

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he filled in the handbreadth, or removed his stones, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The second person undoes his own addition: he fills in the extra טפח he dug, or takes away the stones from רבא's case.

phrases.english: Do we say:
what he did – he has taken away;
or perhaps,
the action of the first one has been removed,
and the whole pit now stands in his domain?
phrases.notes: 'His' means the second person, who would now be responsible for the whole pit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָבָא: טָם טֶפַח, וְסִילֵּק אֲבָנָיו, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from completing the pit to the opposite case, where the completer undoes his addition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: After the second person undoes his addition, does responsibility go back to the first digger, or does the second person keep responsibility for the whole pit?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבא's question without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends by saying רבא's question has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides of the question stay possible. We do not know whether undoing the addition brings back the first digger's responsibility or leaves the whole pit on the second person.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's question about the person who undoes his addition is left as a תיקו: no answer is given.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether responsibility goes back to the first digger after the second undoes his addition remains unresolved.

steps.title: Water counts double toward a pit's depth
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quoting שמואל בר מרתא: a בור eight טפחים deep with two טפחים of water makes the owner liable, because each טפח of water counts like two of dry space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of שמואל בר מרתא: a pit eight handbreadths deep, two of them filled with water, makes the owner liable. Why? Each handbreadth of water counts like two handbreadths of dry space.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: a pit that is less than ten טפחים deep can still count as a deadly pit if it has water in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a בור needs ten טפחים to kill. Here the pit is only eight, but the two טפחים of water each count double, so it adds up to ten. Water adds danger, so it makes up for missing depth.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, a unit of measure

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Shmuel bar Marta said:
A pit eight handbreadths deep,
and two of those handbreadths are water,
he is liable.
What is the reason?
Every handbreadth of water
is like two handbreadths of dry space.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר מָרְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how water affects the ten-טפחים measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pit of eight טפחים with two טפחים of water counts as a deadly pit, because each טפח of water equals two dry טפחים.

steps.title: A pit nine deep with one handbreadth of water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a בור nine טפחים deep with only one טפח of water: does less water mean no deadly air, or does the extra depth make it deadly?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: a pit nine handbreadths deep with one handbreadth of water, what is the law? Do we say that since there is not much water, it has no deadly air? Or maybe since it is deeper, it does have deadly air?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about a case that sits between the rules: by the counting rule it adds up to ten, but it has less water than שמואל's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the 'water counts double' math, eight dry plus one water doubled is ten. But maybe שמואל's rule only works when there is a good amount of water. On the other hand, this pit is deeper than שמואל's case, which might make up for less water.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
The deadly air or fumes inside a pit

phrases.english: They asked:
A pit nine handbreadths deep
and one handbreadth of it is water, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דְּלָא נְפִישִׁי מַיָּא –
phrases.english: Do we say that since there is not much water,
it has no deadly air;
or perhaps, since it is deeper,
it does have deadly air?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far שמואל's rule from step 11 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a pit of nine טפחים with one טפח of water count as deadly: is the amount of water the key, or the depth?

steps.title: A pit seven deep with three handbreadths of water
steps.stepSummary: The opposite question: a בור only seven deep but with three טפחים of water. Does the extra water make it deadly, or is it too shallow?
steps.simpleTranslation: A pit seven handbreadths deep with three handbreadths of water, what is the law? Do we say that since there is more water, it has deadly air? Or maybe since it is not deep, it has no deadly air?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the mirror-image question: now there is more water than in שמואל's case, but less depth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the counting math, four dry plus three water doubled is ten. The question is whether a lot of water can make up for a pit that is quite shallow. Together with step 12, the גמרא is asking which matters more: the amount of water or the actual depth.

phrases.english: A pit seven handbreadths deep,
and three handbreadths of it are water, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֵּיוָן דִּנְפִישִׁי מַיִם טְפֵי –
phrases.english: Do we say that since there is more water,
it has deadly air;
or perhaps, since it is not deep,
it has no deadly air?

steps.triggerLanguage: בּוֹר שִׁבְעָה, וּמֵהֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה טְפָחִים מַיִם, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror image of step 12: more water, less depth.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a pit of seven טפחים with three טפחים of water count as deadly?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends both questions with תיקו: they stay unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the two questions about the nine-deep and seven-deep pits without deciding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only שמואל's exact case (eight with two of water) is settled. The cases with less water and more depth, or more water and less depth, remain a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: Eight טפחים with two of water is a deadly pit. Nine with one of water, or seven with three of water, remain unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions of steps 12 and 13 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The cases of nine-with-one and seven-with-three stay in doubt.

steps.title: What if someone widened the pit?
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי asks רבה what the law is if someone widened a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שיזבי asked רבה: if he widened the pit, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question: instead of making the pit deeper, what if someone makes it wider?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the focus was on depth and deadly air. Now רב שיזבי asks whether making a pit wider counts as adding to the danger, which would make the one who widened it responsible.

phrases.english: Rav Sheizevi asked Rabba:
If he widened it, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from depth and water to a new kind of change: widening.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does widening a pit count as adding to its danger?

steps.title: רבה: widening lessens the deadly air
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that widening actually reduces the הבל, so it does not make the pit worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He has reduced the deadly air.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers that widening is not harmful, because a wider pit has less deadly air.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit kills because of the trapped air at the bottom. When the opening is wider, more fresh air gets in, so the deadly air gets weaker. So by רבה's logic, the one who widened it did not add danger.

phrases.english: He said to him:
He has reduced the deadly air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שיזבי's question from step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Widening lessens the deadly air, so it does not make the pit worse.

steps.title: רב שיזבי: widening brings the danger closer
steps.stepSummary: רב שיזבי pushes back: on the contrary, widening makes the danger closer, since an animal is more likely to fall in.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On the contrary, he has brought the damage closer!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שיזבי challenges רבה's answer, arguing that widening actually makes things worse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looked only at the deadly air. רב שיזבי points to a different danger: a wider opening is easier to fall into. So even if the air is weaker, more animals will fall in, and that adds to the damage.

phrases.english: He said to him: On the contrary,
phrases.notes: Now רב שיזבי is speaking back to רבה.

phrases.english: he has brought the damage closer!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַדְּרַבָּה, הֲרֵי קֵירַב הֶזֵּיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that widening a pit lessens its danger.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Widening may weaken the deadly air, but it makes falling in more likely, so overall it adds to the danger.

steps.title: רב אשי: It depends on how the animal died
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי settles the argument between רבה and רב שיזבי. If the animal died from the הבל, widening helped. If it died from the impact of the fall, widening made things worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: Let us look at it this way. If the animal died from the fumes, then the one who widened it reduced the fumes. If it died from the impact, then he brought the damage closer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי resolves the back-and-forth about widening a בור by saying both sides are right, each in a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said widening reduces the הבל. רב שיזבי said widening makes falling more likely. רב אשי says the answer depends on what actually killed the animal: the fumes (so he is exempt) or the blow of the fall (so he is liable).

keyTerms.meaning: Let us look and see; let us examine the case
The suffocating air or fumes inside a בור
The blow or impact of hitting the bottom

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Let us see:
If it died from the fumes,
then he reduced the fumes;
if it died from the impact,
then he brought the damage closer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: נִיחְזֵי אֲנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the clash between רבה (step 16) and רב שיזבי (step 17) by splitting the cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Widening is always either good (less הבל) or always bad (closer danger).
steps.terutzMaskana: It depends on whether the animal died from the fumes or from the impact.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the law can depend on what actually caused the damage.

steps.title: Another version of רב אשי: It depends on which side the animal fell
steps.stepSummary: Some report רב אשי differently. If the animal fell on the widened side, the widener brought the damage closer. If it fell on the other side, he only reduced the הבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב אשי said, let us see. If it fell on that side, he brought the damage closer. If it fell on the other side, he reduced the fumes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way that רב אשי's answer was reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the test is not how the animal died but where it fell in. Falling into the new widened part means the widening caused the fall, so he is liable. Falling in from the old side means his widening only made the air less deadly.
steps.whatToRemember: Widening a בור: in one version the answer depends on fumes versus impact, and in the other on which side the animal fell in.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
Rav Ashi said: Let us see:
if it fell on that side,
phrases.notes: "That side" means the side he widened.

phrases.english: then he brought the damage closer;
and if it fell on the other side,
then he reduced the fumes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: נִיחְזֵי אֲנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternate report of the same resolution by רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing by location of the fall
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The deciding factor is the cause of death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The deciding factor is which side of the בור the animal fell from.

steps.title: A בור whose depth equals its width
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף both quote רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי מני, but they report him differently. One says such a בור has הבל unless it is wider than it is deep. The other says it has no הבל unless it is deeper than it is wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: About a pit whose depth equals its width, רבה and רב יוסף both speak in the name of רבה בר בר חנה, who spoke in the name of רבי מני. One says: it always has fumes, unless its width is more than its depth. The other says: it never has fumes, unless its depth is more than its width.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute: does a בור that is exactly as deep as it is wide count as having deadly הבל?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree on the clear cases: a deeper-than-wide pit has הבל, and a wider-than-deep pit does not. They disagree only about the equal case. The first opinion makes the digger liable there, and the second exempts him.
steps.confusionAlert: Both opinions quote the same teacher with the same words "עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא". The whole difference is which way the default goes when depth and width are equal.

phrases.english: It was stated:
a pit whose depth is like its width:
Rabba and Rav Yosef both say
in the name of Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
who says it in the name of Rabbi Mani;

phrases.aramaic: חַד אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם יֵשׁ בָּהּ הֶבֶל,
phrases.english: one says: it always has fumes,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא רׇחְבָּהּ יָתֵר עַל עוֹמְקָהּ;
phrases.english: unless its width is more than its depth;

phrases.aramaic: וְחַד אָמַר: לְעוֹלָם אֵין בָּהּ הֶבֶל,
phrases.english: and one says: it never has fumes,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא עוֹמְקָהּ יָתֵר עַל רׇחְבָּהּ.
phrases.english: unless its depth is more than its width.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of הבל in a בור with a new case about proportions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dispute: when depth equals width, one opinion says it has הבל (liable) and the other says it has none (exempt).

steps.title: From when is the first partner no longer responsible?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the first partner passing by an uncovered בור. It asks at what exact moment the first partner is released from responsibility.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the first passed by it and did not cover it. And from when is the first exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line in the משנה and sets up a question about timing. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that once the second partner takes over, he is liable and the first is not. The גמרא wants the precise point of handover: when does responsibility pass from the first to the second?

phrases.english: The first passed by it and did not cover it.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה about two partners sharing a בור.

phrases.english: And from when is the first exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הבל discussion and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact moment responsibility passes from the first partner to the second.

steps.title: Two answers: when he leaves it in use, or when he hands over his bucket
steps.stepSummary: Again רבה and רב יוסף quote רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי מני, and again they report him differently. One says the first partner is exempt once he leaves the second partner using the בור. The other says only once he hands over his bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say in the name of רבה בר בר חנה, who said in the name of רבי מני: one says, from when he leaves him using it. The other says, from when he hands him his bucket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with two opinions about the moment of handover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, it is enough that the second partner is already using the בור when the first walks away. In the second view, responsibility only passes with a clear act of handing over the bucket.

keyTerms.meaning: From when he leaves him while he is using it

phrases.english: Rabba and Rav Yosef both say
in the name of Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
who says it in the name of Rabbi Mani;
one says: from when he leaves him using it,
and one says: from when he hands him his bucket.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the timing question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dispute: either once he leaves the second partner using the בור, or only once he hands over his bucket.

steps.title: The same dispute appears among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this dispute matches a ברייתא. The תנא קמא says the first person is exempt once he leaves the other using the בור. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only once he hands over his bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like a dispute of תנאים: someone is drawing water from a pit, and his friend comes and tells him, "Let me, and I will draw water." Once he leaves him using it, he is exempt. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: from when he hands him his bucket.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the two אמוראic opinions match an earlier dispute between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes the same handover situation. The first opinion matches "leaves him using it", and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב matches "hands over his bucket." So each אמורא's version has a תנא behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: Leave it to me; let me

steps.whatToRemember: When responsibility for an open בור passes to the next user is an old dispute. Either it passes once he is left using it, or only when the bucket is handed over (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

phrases.english: This is like a dispute of tanna'im:
one who is drawing water from a pit,
and his friend came and said to him:
Leave it to me, and I will draw water;
once he leaves him using it, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: "Exempt" here means the first person is no longer responsible if the בור is left uncovered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
from when he hands him his bucket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the אמוראic dispute in step 22 matches a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: The two opinions of רבה and רב יוסף about when the first partner is exempt.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא (once he leaves him using it) against רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (once he hands over his bucket).

steps.title: The root of the dispute is ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the two sides of the ברייתא really disagree about. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds יש ברירה, so each partner draws his own water. The רבנן hold אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they disagree about? רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds there is ברירה: this one draws from his own share, and that one draws from his own share. The רבנן hold there is no ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea is behind the dispute from Step 23. It answers that the two sides disagree about ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יש ברירה, the water each partner draws is treated as having been his own share all along. So while the first partner still draws, part of the water in the בור is still his, and he stays responsible until he hands over his bucket. With אין ברירה, all the water is shared, so once the first partner leaves the second one using the בור, the second one is in charge.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they disagree about? (asks for the idea behind a dispute)
There is ברירה: what is chosen later shows what was yours from the start
There is no ברירה: a later choice does not show what was yours from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Each opinion is tied to the person who holds it, so match them carefully. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (yes ברירה) is the one who says the first partner is exempt only once he hands over his bucket. The רבנן (no ברירה) say he is exempt as soon as he leaves.
steps.whyThisMatters: ברירה is a basic idea found all over the תלמוד, in many areas of הלכה. Here it shows up in נזיקין.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means the תנא קמא and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב from the ברייתא in Step 23.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov holds:
there is designation after the fact —
this one is filling from his own share,
and that one is filling from his own share.
And the Rabbis hold: there is no designation after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the ברייתא dispute brought in Step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute depends on ברירה: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds יש ברירה, and the רבנן hold אין ברירה.

steps.title: רבינא: the same sides disagree about partners with a נדר
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says these תנאים are consistent with what they hold elsewhere. He brings the משנה about partners who made a נדר not to benefit from each other and whether they may enter their shared חצר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: they follow their own reasoning, as we learned in a משנה: partners who made a נדר not to benefit from each other may not enter the חצר. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: this one enters into his own part, and that one enters into his own part.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second case where the same two sides disagree. This sets up the next step, which explains that this dispute is also about ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two partners own one חצר together, and each made a נדר not to get any benefit from the other. The רבנן forbid them to walk in, because every spot is partly owned by the other partner. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב allows it, because each one is walking in his own part.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning, the same way they hold elsewhere
Made a נדר not to get any benefit

phrases.english: Ravina said:
And they follow their own reasoning,
as we learned in a mishna:
partners who vowed not to benefit from each other —
are forbidden to enter the courtyard.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
this one enters into his own part,
and that one enters into his own part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברירה dispute from Step 24 also appears in another משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The two sides hold the same views on ברירה in other places as well.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נדרים about partners who made a נדר not to benefit from each other.

steps.title: The חצר dispute is also about ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the נדרים dispute the same way. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds יש ברירה, so each partner enters his own part. The רבנן hold אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do they disagree about? רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds there is ברירה: this one enters for himself, and that one enters for himself. The רבנן hold there is no ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבינא's point. The חצר dispute rests on exactly the same disagreement about ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With יש ברירה, the spot each partner walks on is treated as his own part from the start, so he gets no benefit from the other. With אין ברירה, every spot belongs to both of them, so walking in means using the other partner's property. This matches the בור case exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: For himself, into his own part

steps.whatToRemember: In both of these disputes, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds יש ברירה and the רבנן hold אין ברירה. That one idea explains both the bucket case at the בור and the shared חצר case.

phrases.english: With regard to what do they disagree?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב סָבַר: יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה –
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov holds: there is designation after the fact —
this one enters into his own part,
and that one enters into his own part.
And the Rabbis hold: there is no designation after the fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה from Step 25 and shows that it matches Step 24.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In both cases the same ברירה dispute is at work: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב holds יש ברירה and the רבנן hold אין ברירה.

steps.title: Selling a pit: the buyer acquires once the seller hands over his bucket
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that when someone sells a בור, the buyer acquires it once the seller hands him his bucket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: if someone sells a water pit to another person, once he hands over his bucket, the buyer has acquired the pit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי אלעזר about buying a בור. It connects to the bucket idea from the previous steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier steps, handing over the bucket decided when a partner stopped being responsible. Here the same act decides when a buyer becomes the owner. רבי אלעזר says the bucket handover is the moment of קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: a pit or cistern for holding water
he acquired; the ownership has passed to him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a simple everyday act, handing over a bucket, can carry legal weight in a sale.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
One who sells a pit to his fellow,
once he handed over his bucket to him, he acquired it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הַמּוֹכֵר בּוֹר לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related ruling, because the earlier steps were about handing over a bucket at a בור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer of a בור acquires it once the seller hands him the bucket.

steps.title: Why should the bucket matter? Money or חזקה should do the acquiring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר. If the sale is done with money, the money should acquire. If it is done with חזקה, the buyer's use should acquire. What does the bucket add?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he is buying with money, let him acquire with the money. If he is buying with חזקה, let him acquire with the חזקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the bucket handover fits with the normal ways of acquiring land. It looks like the bucket has no job to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land can be acquired with כסף (money) or with חזקה (acting as the owner). Either way, the קנין should already happen without any bucket. So רבי אלעזר's focus on the bucket seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it work?
money, used as a way of acquiring
acquiring land by acting as its owner, such as using it

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it is with money, let him acquire with the money!
If it is with taking possession, let him acquire with taking possession!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי בְּכַסְפָּא – לִיקְנֵי בְּכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling by asking what job the bucket does.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling that handing over the bucket makes the buyer acquire.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both normal methods, כסף and חזקה, already acquire on their own. So the bucket seems to add nothing.

steps.title: It is חזקה, and the bucket counts as saying 'לך חזק וקני'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sale really is by חזקה. Normally the seller must tell the buyer 'לך חזק וקני'. Handing over the bucket is like saying those words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really it is by חזקה. Normally the seller needs to tell him: 'Go, take possession and acquire.' Once he hands him his bucket, it is as if he told him: 'Go, take possession and acquire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The bucket is not the קנין itself. It is the seller's permission for the buyer to make a חזקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חזקה, the buyer's use only acquires if the seller agrees to it. Usually this agreement is said out loud: 'לך חזק וקני'. Handing over the bucket shows the same agreement, so when the buyer draws water, his חזקה works.

keyTerms.meaning: actually, really (keeping one side of the question)
'Go, take possession and acquire' — the seller's permission for a חזקה
it is as if he said

steps.whatToRemember: The bucket is not a new way of acquiring. It is the seller's permission, like saying 'לך חזק וקני', and the buyer acquires through his own חזקה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the bucket handover alone is the קנין. It only stands in for the seller's words. The real קנין is the חזקה when the buyer uses the pit.

phrases.english: Actually, it is with taking possession,
and he needs to say to him:
"Go, take possession and acquire";
and once he handed over his bucket to him,

phrases.aramaic: כְּמַאן דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ ״לֵךְ חֲזֵק וּקְנֵי״ דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: it is as if he said to him "Go, take possession and acquire."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by choosing the חזקה side and explaining what the bucket does.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case: the sale is by חזקה, and the bucket counts as the seller's permission.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bucket seemed to be a pointless extra step, because כסף or חזקה should acquire by themselves.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חזקה needs the seller's 'לך חזק וקני', and handing over the bucket counts as that permission.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that permission for a חזקה can be shown by an action, not only said in words.

steps.title: A new ruling begins: selling a house
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי begins a ruling about someone who sells a house. The rest of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: one who sells a house to his fellow...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It starts a related ruling from רבי יהושע בן לוי about selling a house, and the ruling itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like רבי אלעזר's ruling about the בור, this is about a sale and when responsibility or ownership passes. Only the opening case is given here, so we do not know the ruling yet.

keyTerms.meaning: to his fellow, to another person

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who sells a house to his fellow,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הַמּוֹכֵר בַּיִת לַחֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel ruling about a different sale, a house instead of a בור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. Only the case of selling a house is introduced, and the ruling continues past this point.
